title: OMRS pathology features associate with oral-leukoplakia progression
summary: A modified Inception-v3 model learned normal and malignant oral-epithelium features, then scored leukoplakia slides from 62 patients without concurrent cancer. The high-score group had a reported adjusted hazard ratio of 4.52 for progression to oral cancer. This was a small retrospective prognostic analysis; the classifier used a separate 38-biopsy development set, and broader clinical utility and treatment benefit remain untested.
organization: University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center; University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center

source_review.scope: Primary full paper relevant model Methods, study Results and limitations; exact primary front-matter identity and Europe PMC metadata checked.

evidence.tested: Slide-separated development and 62-patient retrospective progression analysis; adjusted hazard ratio 4.52.
evidence.unknown: Small training/cohort sizes, external transportability and intervention benefits remain unresolved.
evidence.ai_role: Modified Inception-v3 classifies oral histology patches, quantifies tumor-like epithelium in leukoplakia and links scores to subsequent clinical progression.
